item.title: Solved: How to Calculate MD5 Hash of Large Files in Python
item.description:
In today's data-driven world, efficiently computing the MD5 hash of large files in Python poses a common challenge. If you've encountered issues when dealing with files that might not fit into your system's RAM, you're not alone. Here, we will explore various effective techniques to generate the MD5 hash of such files without overwhelming your memory capacity. This guide aims to provide you with practical, tested methods for handling large data efficiently using Python's built-in capabilities.

### How to Efficiently Compute MD5 Hash of Large Files in Python

When hashing large files, it is critical to avoid loading the entire file into memory. Below are practical methods employing chunk reading, which limits the memory usage to a mere chunk at a time:

## Method 1: Using Chunk Reading with `update()`

One fundamental approach is to process the file in manageable pieces. The following example demonstrates how to achieve this through 8192-byte chunking:

```python
import hashlib

def calculate_md5_large_file(filepath):
    file_hash = hashlib.md5()
    with open(filepath, "rb") as file:
        while chunk := file.read(8192):  # Read the file in chunks
            file_hash.update(chunk)       # Update the hash with the chunk
    return file_hash.hexdigest()        # Returns the hash as a hexadecimal string

## Example usage:
hash_value = calculate_md5_large_file("your_large_file.txt")
print(f"MD5 Hash: {hash_value}")

This method keeps memory consumption low while allowing you to process large files efficiently.
